page_title: Building Blockchain in Go. Part 3: Persistence and CLI - Going the distance

summary.title: Building Blockchain in Go. Part 3: Persistence and CLI
summary.one_liner: You learn how to persist a Go blockchain in BoltDB using gob serialization, iterate stored blocks, and expose addblock and printchain commands through a small CLI.
keywords: proof of work blockchain series part 3
takeaways: BoltDB is a simple pure-Go key/value store where keys and values are byte arrays, organized in buckets, with no server required.
Blocks are serialized with encoding/gob before being stored, and deserialized when read back.
The blockchain is persisted by storing blocks keyed by hash plus an 'l' key pointing to the last block hash (tip); reopening the DB resumes the chain.
A BlockchainIterator walks blocks from tip to genesis one at a time, avoiding loading the whole chain into memory.
A minimal CLI built on the standard flag package provides addblock -data and printchain subcommands.
summary.summary: The article is Part 3 of a series building a blockchain in Go. It explains why BoltDB was chosen over alternatives, how Bitcoin Core lays out its LevelDB buckets, and then implements a simplified schema with a single blocks bucket. The author walks through gob-based Serialize/DeserializeBlock, rewrites NewBlockchain and AddBlock to use read-write and read-only BoltDB transactions, and adds a BlockchainIterator. It closes with a CLI using Go's flag package, with sample terminal output showing the genesis block and added blocks.
